the force-displacement curves for pit membranes of never-dried and dried Larix and Pinu s earlywood pits were similar and that the force-displacements curves of never-dried pits were similar to those of aspirated pits.

the elastic modulus of pit membranes of never-dried earlywood bordered pits of Larix and P. sylvestris is in the range of 0.1 to 1.5 GPa, with the lower end of the range corresponding to torus prolapse failure mode, and the higher end of the range to membrane rupture failure.

the pit membranes of Larix and P. taeda earlywood are very stiff and strong, and that the pit membranes are more susceptible to rupture or tearing when the torus is in a retracted position, and more resistant to failure when the torus has prolapsed into the pit chamber.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the force-displacement measurements are useful in characterizing the mechanical behavior of pit membranes, and that the force-displacements for the two failure modes of pit membrane failure are different.

The main takeaway from our work is that

pit membrane failure is not a simple process, but rather is highly dependent on the geometry of the pit membrane, the material properties of the pit membrane and torus, and the loading conditions applied to the pit membrane.

pit membrane failure is not a simple function of membrane thickness, but rather is influenced by the mechanical strength of the pit membrane, which is a function of both thickness and material composition.

the mesomechanical system can be used to measure the mechanical properties of pit membranes and that the system is capable of generating force-displacement curves for both rupture and torus prolapse failure modes.
